title: The Fantasy World Simulator — Design Reference Wiki

pages.title: A Run, Start to Finish
pages.blurb: The shape of a whole run — remembrance and your two domains, the opening spine and The First, the middle game, how either clock ends the run, and what the World-Soul carries into the next.

pages.title: Reaches, Spheres & Quintessence
pages.blurb: The two axes of every divine act — Eight Reaches (what you do) and Twelve Spheres (what fuels it), orthogonal by design — plus each Reach's virtue/vice moral axis, the Domain Capability word-ladder, and Quintessence as narrative centrality (not a ninth Reach).

pages.title: The Three-Beat Turn
pages.blurb: How a turn works — the world waits until you advance it; each turn runs scan → curated moment → aftermath in a load-bearing order; time in ticks (two hours, twelve per day); and encounters as rationed chapters, not per-tick rolls.

pages.title: Divine Actions & Prerequisites
pages.blurb: The five verbs every divine act reduces to (Create/Find/Change/Destroy/Control), why some action cards never appear (Reach outside your two domains — permanent; sphere misalignment; too little capability), the Generalized Action Targeting cascade, and the two reach signatures you acquire as story moments.

pages.title: Threads, the Court & The First
pages.blurb: The thread as a two-way bond — your investment depth (the five influence tiers) versus the mortal's awareness (unaware → intuition → faith → communion); the four court positions; The First's doom-clock-scheduled hero's journey; familiarity as player-side progressive disclosure; and why holding a thread deeply costs upkeep and makes you louder to rivals.

pages.title: Essence, Control & Sustained Power
pages.blurb: Divine fuel is per-Sphere and tight on purpose — where essence comes from (a baseline flow, worshippers, places of power, an Aspect's conduit) and how it splits along your alignment (0.35/0.25/0.40); Control as sustained commitment (upkeep, the slot cap, the three ways a working lapses); the usurp/destroy contestation trade where age is the defence; and the long strategic works that erode when neglected.

pages.title: Encounters & Aftermath
pages.blurb: The encounter as a framed chapter, not a die roll — the two shapes (branching and recurring) that share one UnifiedActionTemplate format; hex-granular awareness (see the hex, see everything on it); the single sigmoid→d100 resolution curve for peasants and gods, with doubles-based crits; aftermath as the mortal's trajectory shift; failure as plot; and the four encounter design rules. Player-voice layer over the deep encounters-agents-reference page.

pages.title: Doom, the Mandate & Omens
pages.blurb: The two clocks that pressure every run from opposite directions — the Doom Clock (seven archetypes, five Whispers→Culmination stages, escalations as world events) counting down to an Unmaking that always lands, and the Victory Mandate (three stages, your declared win-state) counting up; the one-pool-two-clocks tension made concrete by mandate checkpoints that bank counter-omens or owe doom severity; and omens as the pressure made visible.

pages.title: Reading the Interface
pages.blurb: A guided tour of the game screen — the one-viewport, no-scroll contract; the always-on frame (essence, the two clocks, omens, attention, identity, rivals); the drill-in from hex to location to sublocation; the panels (threads, retinue, chronicle, narrative feed); the Action Drawer; the encounter surfaces and the deeper sheets; and a cross-reference from every other Manual page to the surface where its system shows its face. Source spine is the IA manifest (62 surfaces).

pages.title: The Mortals
pages.blurb: The mortals who fill the world and pursue their own goals — how a free mortal chooses (a Maslow-inspired, survival-first, values-driven seeded selection, not a literal six-tier ladder); the nine virtue↔flaw value pairs (eight Reach-bound plus courage/prudence) and the slow moral drift a god can bend; ambitions in seven shapes; growth through doing and the five ways a mentorship ends; and the lifecycle from birth to death and the ambient→notable→spotlight graduation that turns a background face into a named individual.

pages.title: Factions, Cultures & Secrets
pages.blurb: The social fabric over the mortals — factions as bodies with their own designs (per-faction reputation ladders, autonomous ambitions and actions, mortal succession, schism, and the chosen-faction anointing); cultures as gravity wells you are born inside of (venerated Spheres, generated names and mores, cultural gravity and the four tensions); and the unseen currency of secrets and favors that tilt a social encounter before a word is spoken.

pages.title: The World: Hexes, Terrain & Sight
pages.blurb: The world as a grid of hexes you can shape — the three nested tiers of place (hex → location → sublocation, one rung at a time); terrain and how divine influence, corruption, and per-location magical saturation remake it; and the two hex-distance sight systems, the god's fog of war (unexplored → visible → remembered) and each mortal's own encounter awareness. Load-bearing: hexes are flat array state, not graph nodes.

pages.title: Settlements, Prosperity & Trade
pages.blurb: How settlements rise and fall on their own — the four tiers (hamlet → town → city, with capital fixed) and the sustained-prosperity thresholds that promote or demote them; prosperity as an equilibrium value drifting toward conditions and unrest as a settlement's instability; trade routes that decay when un-travelled; and terrain-seeded resources plus rare anomalies that set a place's ceiling. Honest scope: the economy is texture serving story, not a trading sim.

pages.title: Livelihoods & the Resource Web
pages.blurb: The activated resource economy (Phase 1) — how every place's Livelihood reads in prose from its resource stock tiers (scarce/adequate/surplus), when a staple crosses into Famine or Glut, how supply-vs-demand balance nudges prosperity, how a bonded mortal's home turning hungry pulls a livelihood thread tug, and the resource-class table that leans each good toward a Sphere. Companion to the settlements page; honest scope: P1 activates the layer, trade cargo and divine verbs come later.

pages.title: Armies, Battles & Lairs
pages.blurb: War as a story generator, not a wargame — armies that factions raise for conquest or revenge (three sizes, terrain-punished marches, Quintessence-cohesion attrition and its four threshold encounters); field battles that resolve as a momentum struggle over several turns, tilted by thread-gated spotlights and leaving destruction, captured commanders, and refugees in their wake; sieges as an accelerating battle subtype where walls favour the defender and starvation the attacker; and monster lairs that escalate minor → major (named elite) → legendary (monster faction), poison the land, and reinfest if cleared ground is left untended.

pages.title: Encounters, Agents & Resolution
pages.blurb: Eight Reaches, Domain Capability, species, traits, attachments, the encounter types, the resolution pipeline, divine intervention, and the agent decision pipeline.

pages.title: Tick Cycle Reference
pages.blurb: All 12 orchestrator acts and 40+ phases in tick order, each with its reads, writes, and RNG tags.

pages.title: Action Catalog
pages.blurb: Browsable, code-true catalog of every ascendant-facing action template — spheres, reaches, costs, availability buckets, and authored technical game-effects with a derived wiring badge.
